properties.rop_renaming_meaning: Sue-meg is the Yurok name for this coast, used since time immemorial. The former name honored Patrick Beegan, an 1850s settler later implicated in violence against Native Americans.
properties.description: In 2021, Sue-meg became the first site renamed under California State Parks' Reexamining Our Past initiative, restoring the Yurok place name in place of Patrick's Point.
properties.compare_source: T. T. Waterman, Yurok Geography (1920), Rectangle J

properties.description: A reconstructed Yurok village - dance house, sweat house, changing houses, family houses, and a redwood canoe - planned and built by Yurok people with park staff. Although permanent villages lay north and south, the Sue-meg area itself was primarily a seasonal encampment.
properties.caption: Sumeg Village, rebuilt in the 1990s - a living cultural site, not a museum exhibit.

properties.description: A Yurok place name for the larger of the Turtle Rocks near Sue-meg. Waterman recorded this offshore sea-stack as “harbor-seal his rock,” while the Yurok Language Project gives the modern form as Chkweges ’W-a’aag, “seals’ rock.”
properties.caption: Turtle Rocks
